title: Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District general election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the U.S. House member for a district covering much of southern Wisconsin, including Madison, Monroe, Dodgeville, and Baraboo. Incumbent Democrat Mark Pocan, first elected in 2012, is seeking re-election and faces a Democratic primary challenge from Douglas Alexander. Notably, no Republican candidate filed to run in this heavily Democratic-leaning district, meaning the Democratic primary winner will be unopposed in the general election. The district has not been competitive since 2000, with recent Republican nominees receiving around 30% of the vote.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District in 2026 were found. The district is rated Safe/Solid D by all major nonpartisan forecasters.

candidates.name: Mark Pocan
candidates.summary: Mark Pocan is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2012. He previously served 14 years in the Wisconsin State Assembly and is a co-chair of the Congressional LGBTQ+ Equality Caucus. Pocan is running for re-election on a platform focused on labor rights, healthcare access, and progressive economic policies.

candidates.name: Douglas Alexander
candidates.summary: Douglas Alexander is a Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Mark Pocan in the August 11, 2026 primary for Wisconsin's 2nd Congressional District. A former teacher and Madison native, Alexander is running primarily on a platform of congressional term limits, advocating for a constitutional amendment limiting House members to three terms and Senators to two terms. He has run for this seat previously as an independent in 2022.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polls are available. This forecast relies entirely on race context: Wisconsin's 2nd District is heavily Democratic and has not been competitive since 2000. Critically, no Republican candidate filed to run in 2026, so the Democratic primary winner will be unopposed in the general election, guaranteeing a Democratic hold. Incumbent Mark Pocan (first elected 2012) is strongly favored to win the August 11 Democratic primary over challenger Douglas Alexander, who ran as an independent in 2022 and lacks significant institutional support or fundraising. The only meaningful uncertainty is the primary outcome, but incumbency advantages, name recognition, and progressive credentials make Pocan the clear favorite. Party probability for Democratic is set at 1.0 because the general election has no opposing-party candidate; the margin estimate reflects the district's typical Democratic vote share (~65+ points) against a hypothetical opponent, as recent Republican nominees received around 30%.
